territorial_scope.description: Applies to United States federal government bodies, including the Department of Defense, the intelligence community, the Coast Guard and other federal agencies; subtitle B excludes intelligence community elements.

summary.short: Selected AI-related sections of the FY2023 National Defense Authorization Act govern Department of Defense, intelligence community, Coast Guard and federal-agency AI adoption through reports, designated officials, pilots, workforce and acquisition provisions, generally running from enactment.
summary.long: The text provided is a set of AI-related sections of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, not the full Act. It directs the Department of Defense, the intelligence community, the Coast Guard and other federal agencies on AI adoption. Section 212 and related sections replace references to the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center with an official designated under section 238(b) of the FY2019 NDAA. Section 1513 requires the Deputy Secretary of Defense to establish priority data and AI projects. Section 6702 requires the Director of National Intelligence to set AI policies and standards and to designate element leads, and sections 6717, 6721 and 6723 add metrics, reports and workforce plans. Subtitle B (Advancing American AI Act, section 7224) sets OMB-directed rules for federal AI acquisition, privacy and security, and section 7225 requires agencies to prepare AI use-case inventories and make them available to the public, excluding DoD. Section 7226 requires four AI use-case pilots, with a five-year sunset. Section 11226 requires a Coast Guard designated official and a strategic plan. Several duties have deadlines counted from enactment, such as 60, 180 or 270 days, or one or two years. Section 7228 excludes intelligence community elements from subtitle B.Workforce, scholarship and cybersecurity training provisions (sections 1535, 6723, 9506, 835) also appear in the excerpt.

notes: Excerpt record: the text is a set of AGORA-labelled sections of the FY2023 NDAA rather than the full Act; relations cover only this text, so extent should be partial. Some amending clauses are garbled in extraction (e.g., sec. 212(i) reads Section 808 the William M.; sec. 6505(f) gives the CHIPS Act Public Law citation as 117- followed by 1.). Sec. 835(c) refers to Such plan with no plan in the excerpt, and sec. 835(d) and (e) refer to the plan in subsection (d) although it is described in subsection (c); this is an internal inconsistency. Sec. 6717 uses covered product, which the excerpt does not define. Sec. 1554(c) refers to section 1509, which is not included. Target instrument IDs are null because the registry was not checked.
